info.title: Crawmatic API
info.description:
Monitor your competitors' prices for your own products.

Authenticate every request with your workspace API key:

    Authorization: Bearer ck_your_key_here

List endpoints are cursor-paginated and return `{"items": [...], "next_cursor": ...}`; pass `next_cursor` back as `?cursor=` to fetch the next page. Errors always carry a top-level `{"error": {"code", "message"}}` object. Rate limits are 60 read and 10 write requests per minute per key; exceeding them returns 429 with a `Retry-After` header.

post.description:
Set-based bulk upsert (`contracts/catalog-bulk-upsert.md`, FR-010/011/012).

Woo/Salla-style nested payload: dedup last-wins -> resolve identity
(`external_id` -> `sku`) -> a bounded number of
`ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE` statements via `app_shared.catalog.upsert`
(never one statement per product) -> default-variant injection for
any product arriving with zero explicit variants -> a bounded number
of variant upsert statements. Runs entirely inside the request's
workspace-scoped session/transaction (FR-016).

Limitation (FR-011): a product supplied with neither ``external_id``
nor ``sku`` has no identity for ``ON CONFLICT`` matching, so it is
always inserted fresh on every call -- re-pushing an unmodified
identity-less product creates a duplicate row rather than being a
no-op. Callers that want idempotent upsert semantics must supply at
least one of those two fields on every product they intend to keep
in sync (see ``app.schemas.catalog.ProductBulkUpsertItem``).

get.description:
`GET /v1/variants/{variant_id}/price-comparison` (SPEC-09 US1, FR-017/FR-020).

404s an unknown/cross-workspace variant (checked first, via
`scoped_get`) and, separately, a variant that has never been
analyzed yet (no `variant_price_states` row) — both distinguishable
only by message, not status code (contracts/api-alerts.md).

post.description:
Set-based standalone variant bulk upsert (`contracts/catalog-bulk-upsert.md`).

Each row names its parent product by `product_id` /
`product_external_id` / `product_sku`; parent resolution is one
scoped lookup (never per-row). A cross-workspace or unresolvable
parent reference is rejected (422) via the workspace-consistency
pre-check (FR-009) before any upsert statement runs.

Set-based bulk upsert (`contracts/matches-bulk-upsert.md`, FR-013, SC-006).

Flow, per the contract: `prepare_match_urls` (collect `rejected`) ->
`dedup_last_wins` (in-batch last-wins on the 4-col match key) ->
resolve variants via one scoped `IN (...)` lookup (unresolved -> a
single `422`) -> competitor consistency pre-check (one narrow
`IN (...)` lookup + `assert_refs_in_workspace`) ->
`build_matches_upsert` executed once. Never a per-row loop.

Set-based bulk upsert (FR-020, SC-008): `prepare_profiles` (validate +
reject-and-report + last-wins dedup) -> `build_profiles_upsert`
executed once under the caller's workspace context. Tenant-only —
never writes a global row.

put.description:
Set (or, with `profile_id: null`, clear) the caller's workspace
default scrape profile (FR-012/FR-013). `assert_profile_assignable`
accepts own-workspace or global; rejects a cross-workspace reference
(`422 WORKSPACE_MISMATCH`) or a dangling id (`404 NOT_FOUND`).
`Workspace` carries no RLS (root/tenant table) — fetched by plain PK.

get.description: `GET /v1/alerts/current/{variant_id}` — the one current alert row, or 404.

post.description:
`POST /v1/webhook-endpoints` — SSRF-validate `url`, encrypt `secret`
if present, persist scoped to the caller's workspace (FR-002/003/005).

patch.description:
`PATCH /v1/webhook-endpoints/{id}` — partial update; `url` re-validated
when present; `secret` is tri-state (omitted=unchanged, null=clear,
value=re-encrypt); `updated_at` advances via `TimestampMixin.onupdate`
(FR-004). Not in workspace -> 404.

delete.description:
`DELETE /v1/webhook-endpoints/{id}` — hard delete; 204 on success; not
in workspace -> 404 (subsequent get/list absent).

get.description: Liveness probe. Returns 200 whenever the process is serving.

AccessMethod.title: AccessMethod
AccessMethod.description:
Transport method used for a fetch attempt (SPEC-07 §11/§22).

This slice (``generic_price_spider``) writes only ``DIRECT_HTTP`` —
the other members are forward-compat for proxy/browser transports
added by later specs.

AdapterKey.title: AdapterKey
AdapterKey.description: Extraction adapter of a ``scrape_profiles`` row (SPEC-06 §22, FR-001).

AlertEventResponse.title: AlertEventResponse
AlertEventResponse.description: A `price_alert_events` row — one recorded alert transition.

AlertEventType.title: AlertEventType
AlertEventType.description:
Ordered alert-transition classification of a ``price_alert_events`` row (SPEC-09 D5).

``UNCHANGED`` is part of the vocabulary but is never persisted — a
row is written only on a type/severity change (CREATED/UPDATED/
RESOLVED/REOPENED).

AlertSeverity.title: AlertSeverity
AlertSeverity.description: Severity derived solely from ``AlertType`` via the fixed map (SPEC-09 FR-011).

AlertStateResponse.title: AlertStateResponse
AlertStateResponse.description: A `variant_alert_states` row — the current alert for one variant.

AlertStatus.title: AlertStatus
AlertStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of a ``variant_alert_states`` row (SPEC-09 §22).

``ACTIVE`` while the current type is non-``NORMAL``; ``RESOLVED``
(with ``resolved_at`` stamped) once the type returns to ``NORMAL``.

AlertType.title: AlertType
AlertType.description:
Deterministic alert classification of a variant's price position (SPEC-09 §23, FR-004).

Produced by the pure ``app_shared.alerts.engine`` ordered decision
tree; ``NO_COMPETITOR_DATA`` when there is no comparable competitor
price, ``RISK``/``HIGH_PRICE`` when the client price is above the
highest/cheapest competitor, ``CHANCE_TO_INCREASE_PRICE`` when the
client price is more than 5% below the competitor average,
``NORMAL`` within the 1%-5% band, ``CLOSE_TO_COMPETITORS`` under 1%.

CompetitorCreate.title: CompetitorCreate
CompetitorCreate.description:
`POST /v1/competitors` request body.

`name`/`domain` are required; every other field is optional and
falls back to the ORM column default when omitted (`status=ACTIVE`,
`legal_status=REVIEW_REQUIRED`, `robots_policy=RESPECT`).

CompetitorResponse.title: CompetitorResponse
CompetitorResponse.description: A `competitors` row as returned by the API.

CompetitorStatus.title: CompetitorStatus
CompetitorStatus.description: Lifecycle status of a ``competitors`` row (SPEC-05 FR-016).

DeleteOutcome.title: DeleteOutcome
DeleteOutcome.description:
`DELETE` response body (FR-017): reports which outcome occurred.

No dependent history exists yet in this spec, so every delete is
currently `"hard_deleted"`; the shape is structured so a future
archive-by-status path can return `"archived"` without a response
schema change.

DiscoveryRunResponse.title: DiscoveryRunResponse
DiscoveryRunResponse.description: One `strategy_discovery_runs` row, as returned by the API.

DiscoveryRunStatus.title: DiscoveryRunStatus
DiscoveryRunStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of a ``strategy_discovery_runs`` row (SPEC-12 US3 AS1/AS4).

``PENDING`` (enqueued, not yet picked up) → ``RUNNING`` (sample is
being probed) → ``COMPLETED`` (a winning access + extraction method
pair was found, ``winning_*``/``completed_at`` set) or ``NO_WINNER``
(no combination cleared the promotion-quality bar, ``completed_at``
set, ``winning_*`` stay ``NULL``) or ``FAILED`` (an out-of-bounds
``sample_size`` or an unexpected error aborted the run before/
during probing).

DomainAccessRuleCreate.title: DomainAccessRuleCreate
DomainAccessRuleCreate.description:
`POST /v1/domain-access-rules` request body (full FR-004 field set).

Tenant-only — `workspace_id` is never client-supplied; the router
always stamps the caller's own workspace.

DomainAccessRuleResponse.title: DomainAccessRuleResponse
DomainAccessRuleResponse.description: A `domain_access_rules` row as returned by the API (tenant-only).

ExtractionMethod.title: ExtractionMethod
ExtractionMethod.description:
Strategy that produced a price candidate (SPEC-07 §22, contracts/extraction.md).

This slice writes ``JSON_LD``/``CSS``/``REGEX``/``SINGLE_NUMBER``; the
remaining members are forward-compat for later extraction strategies
(platform JSON APIs, embedded JSON blobs, XPath, Playwright-rendered
pages) so the column never needs a widening migration.

GroupCreate.title: GroupCreate
GroupCreate.description:
`POST /v1/product-groups` request body. ``unique(workspace_id, name)``
duplicate -> `409` (enforced by the router, not here).

GroupItemCreate.title: GroupItemCreate
GroupItemCreate.description:
`POST /v1/product-groups/{id}/items` request body.

Exactly one of `product_id` / `product_variant_id` must be set — the
"exactly one" rule is the pure `app_shared.catalog.consistency.exactly_one_of`
core, reused here (not re-implemented) so the API boundary and any
future non-HTTP caller share one rule (`contracts/workspace-consistency.md`
Layer 2). The referenced entity must additionally resolve inside the
caller's workspace — that check runs in the router (composite-FK-backed,
422/404 on cross-workspace/nonexistent), since it requires a DB lookup
this pure schema validator cannot perform.

GroupItemResponse.title: GroupItemResponse
GroupItemResponse.description: A `product_group_items` row as returned by the API.

GroupResponse.title: GroupResponse
GroupResponse.description: A `product_groups` row (with its member items) as returned by the API.

GroupStatus.title: GroupStatus
GroupStatus.description: Lifecycle status of a ``product_groups`` row (SPEC-04 FR-017).

HealthStatus.title: HealthStatus
HealthStatus.description: Scrape health status of a ``competitor_product_matches`` row (SPEC-05 FR-017).

JobResponse.title: JobResponse
JobResponse.description: `GET /v1/jobs/{job_id}` — a `scrape_jobs` row as returned by the API.

LegalStatus.title: LegalStatus
LegalStatus.description:
Legal review status of a ``competitors`` row (SPEC-05 §22, Principle VI).

Competitors default to ``REVIEW_REQUIRED`` per Constitution Principle VI.

MatchBulkUpsertItem.title: MatchBulkUpsertItem
MatchBulkUpsertItem.description:
One record in `POST /v1/matches/bulk-upsert`.

Same field shape as `MatchCreate` — the variant is named by exactly
one of `product_variant_id`/`variant_external_id`/`variant_sku`
(resolved in-workspace by the router, one scoped lookup for the
whole batch); `competitor_id` + `competitor_url` are always
required. `competitor_url` is safety-validated + normalized per row
(FR-009/FR-013) — an unsafe URL is reported in the response's
`rejected[]`, not raised as an error, so it never aborts the rest of
the batch. Health fields are never client-settable (FR-017).

MatchBulkUpsertResult.title: MatchBulkUpsertResult
MatchBulkUpsertResult.description:
`POST /v1/matches/bulk-upsert` response.

`upserted` counts the safe rows actually written by the single
set-based `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE` statement (SC-006); `rejected`
reports every unsafe-URL row by original batch index, never aborting
the rest of the batch (FR-013).

MatchCreate.title: MatchCreate
MatchCreate.description:
`POST /v1/matches` request body.

The variant is named by exactly one of `product_variant_id` /
`variant_external_id` / `variant_sku` (resolved in-workspace by the
router); `competitor_id` + `competitor_url` are always required.

MatchResponse.title: MatchResponse
MatchResponse.description: A `competitor_product_matches` row as returned by the API.

MatchStatus.title: MatchStatus
MatchStatus.description: Lifecycle status of a ``competitor_product_matches`` row (SPEC-05 FR-016).

MatchUpdate.title: MatchUpdate
MatchUpdate.description:
`PATCH /v1/matches/{id}` — every mutable field optional (partial update).

The variant/competitor/product identity of a match is immutable via
PATCH (create a new match instead); if `competitor_url` changes the
router re-validates + re-derives `normalized_competitor_url`/
`url_pattern`/`url_pattern_version`. Health fields remain
server-owned and are never accepted here.

MethodType.title: MethodType
MethodType.description:
Disambiguates the ``method_name`` vocabulary on a ``strategy_attempt_stats``
row / a ``domain_strategy_profiles`` preferred-method pair (SPEC-12 §22, FR-008).

``method_name`` values are the **reused** ``AccessMethod`` members
when ``method_type=ACCESS`` and the **reused** ``ExtractionMethod``
members when ``method_type=EXTRACTION`` — this enum is not itself a
method vocabulary, just the discriminator (research D1).

ProductBulkUpsertItem.title: ProductBulkUpsertItem
ProductBulkUpsertItem.description:
One product row in `POST /v1/products/bulk-upsert` -- a Woo/Salla-style
nested payload where each product optionally carries its own `variants`.

`price`/`currency` seed the auto-derived default variant exactly like
`ProductCreate`, only when `variants` is empty/absent; a product
arriving with **zero** variants and no `price`/`currency` cannot be
upserted (422) -- see `apps/api/app/routers/products.py`.

ProductBulkUpsertResult.title: ProductBulkUpsertResult
ProductBulkUpsertResult.description:
`POST /v1/products/bulk-upsert` response -- every upserted product
(each carrying >=1 variant, FR-012 tail).

ProductCreate.title: ProductCreate
ProductCreate.description:
`POST /v1/products` request body.

`price`/`currency` are optional here at the schema level (they only
seed the auto-derived default variant); the router enforces that a
product arriving with **no** `variants` MUST supply both (422 per
`contracts/api-products.md`) — a schema-level requirement would
incorrectly also demand them on a product that supplies explicit
`variants` instead.

ProductResponse.title: ProductResponse
ProductResponse.description: A `products` row (with its variants) as returned by the API.

ProductStatus.title: ProductStatus
ProductStatus.description: Lifecycle status of a ``products`` row (SPEC-04 FR-017).

RefreshRuleCreate.title: RefreshRuleCreate
RefreshRuleCreate.description:
`POST /v1/refresh-rules` request body.

`name`/`scope` are required; exactly one of `cron_expression`/
`interval_minutes` must be supplied (`INVALID_CADENCE`/`INVALID_CRON`),
and the scope<->target-id matrix must hold (`SCOPE_TARGET_MISMATCH`) —
both re-checked by the router after confirming the supplied target id
resolves in-workspace (contract "the supplied target id must resolve
in-workspace via `scoped_get`").

RefreshRuleResponse.title: RefreshRuleResponse
RefreshRuleResponse.description: A `refresh_rules` row as returned by the API.

RefreshRuleUpdate.title: RefreshRuleUpdate
RefreshRuleUpdate.description:
`PATCH /v1/refresh-rules/{id}` — every field optional (partial update).

An empty body (no fields set) is rejected by the router with
`422 EMPTY_UPDATE` (`strategy.py` precedent) before this schema's
values are ever applied. The router re-validates cadence/scope on the
**merged** (existing row + this patch) view — not this schema alone,
since e.g. patching only `name` must not require re-supplying cadence.
Includes `enabled` — enable/disable is a PATCH field, not a separate
action subresource (contract).

RobotsPolicy.title: RobotsPolicy
RobotsPolicy.description: robots.txt handling policy of a ``competitors`` row (SPEC-05 §22).

ScrapeErrorCode.title: ScrapeErrorCode
ScrapeErrorCode.description:
Structured error-code vocabulary (Constitution §34, contracts/errors.md).

Shared by ``price_observations``/``request_attempts``/
``match_current_prices.error_code`` and by the scraping-side
fetch-failure classification helpers, so debugging, the later
strategy optimizer, access-policy tuning, and client reporting
share one language. This slice (SPEC-07) emits the first eleven
members; the rest are forward-compat placeholders for proxies,
Playwright, the strategy optimizer, and rate-limiting/legal-review
features owned by later specs — declared now so those specs never
need a widening migration on this column.

ScrapeJobSource.title: ScrapeJobSource
ScrapeJobSource.description:
Trigger-source provenance of a ``scrape_jobs`` row (SPEC-08 §22).

Direct API runs (this spec) record ``API``; the remaining members are
forward-compat for the scheduler/internal/plugin triggers owned by
later specs.

ScrapeJobStatus.title: ScrapeJobStatus
ScrapeJobStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of a ``scrape_jobs`` row (SPEC-08 §22, D6).

``PENDING`` at creation -> ``RUNNING`` (dispatch begins) -> a
deterministic terminal status (``COMPLETED``/``PARTIAL_FAILED``/
``FAILED``). ``CANCELLED`` is a vocabulary member but not produced by
this spec's endpoints.

ScrapeJobType.title: ScrapeJobType
ScrapeJobType.description:
Trigger-type provenance of a ``scrape_jobs`` row (SPEC-08 §22).

Direct API runs (this spec) record ``MANUAL``; the remaining members
are forward-compat for the scheduler/retry/discovery features owned
by later specs.

ScrapeProfileBulkUpsertItem.title: ScrapeProfileBulkUpsertItem
ScrapeProfileBulkUpsertItem.description:
One record in `POST /v1/scrape-profiles/bulk-upsert`.

Same field shape as `ScrapeProfileCreate` — matched on
`(workspace_id, name)`, `workspace_id` always stamped server-side
(never client-supplied, never global).

ScrapeProfileBulkUpsertResult.title: ScrapeProfileBulkUpsertResult
ScrapeProfileBulkUpsertResult.description:
`POST /v1/scrape-profiles/bulk-upsert` response.

`upserted` counts the valid rows actually written by the single
set-based `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE` statement (SC-008); `rejected`
reports every invalid row by original batch index, never aborting
the rest of the batch (FR-020).

ScrapeProfileCreate.title: ScrapeProfileCreate
ScrapeProfileCreate.description:
`POST /v1/scrape-profiles` request body.

`name` is required; every other field falls back to the ORM column
default when omitted. `workspace_id` is never accepted here — the
router always stores the caller's own workspace (never global).

ScrapeProfileMode.title: ScrapeProfileMode
ScrapeProfileMode.description: Extraction transport mode of a ``scrape_profiles`` row (SPEC-06 §22, FR-001).

ScrapeProfileResponse.title: ScrapeProfileResponse
ScrapeProfileResponse.description:
A `scrape_profiles` row as returned by the API.

`workspace_id` is `null` for a global (shared) profile — surfaced
verbatim so a caller can distinguish its own rows from globals.

ScrapeScope.title: ScrapeScope
ScrapeScope.description:
Refresh/job scope of a ``scrape_jobs`` row (SPEC-08 §22 "Refresh scopes").

Shared with ``refresh_rules`` in a later spec. This spec's endpoints
(run-match / run-variant) produce only ``MATCH`` and ``VARIANT``; the
remaining members are forward-compat for later scope-run endpoints.

ScrapeTargetStatus.title: ScrapeTargetStatus
ScrapeTargetStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of a ``scrape_job_targets`` row (SPEC-08 §22).

``PENDING`` at creation -> ``STARTED`` -> a terminal status
(``COMPLETED``/``FAILED``/``SKIPPED``). ``mark_target``
(``app_shared.jobs.targets``) is the single writer of these
transitions.

``DEFERRED`` (SPEC-11 FR-018, data-model.md §2.1) is a distinct,
**non-terminal** overflow outcome: an in-spider requeue-cap
overflow hands the target back to Celery ``scrape_dispatch`` for
later re-dispatch (``DEFERRED -> STARTED`` on re-pickup), so it is
deliberately excluded from any terminal-status set.

StrategyProfileDetailResponse.title: StrategyProfileDetailResponse
StrategyProfileDetailResponse.description: A single profile plus its per-method stats (`GET .../profiles/{id}`).

StrategyProfileResponse.title: StrategyProfileResponse
StrategyProfileResponse.description: One `domain_strategy_profiles` row, as returned by the list/get API.

StrategyProfileUpdate.title: StrategyProfileUpdate
StrategyProfileUpdate.description:
`PATCH /v1/strategy/profiles/{id}` operator override body (FR-006/FR-014).

All fields optional; at least one must be provided. `url_pattern` sets a
manual pattern override; `status` may be set to `DISABLED` (stop applying
the learned preference) or back to an active state to re-enable.

StrategyStatus.title: StrategyStatus
StrategyStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of a ``domain_strategy_profiles`` row (SPEC-12 §22, FR-007).

``DISCOVERY_REQUIRED`` (new key, no learned start yet) → ``LEARNING``
(discovery seeded a winner or a promotion attempt is in progress) →
``ACTIVE`` (3-confirmation promotion rule satisfied) → ``DEGRADED``
(rediscovery triggered, FR-020) → back to ``LEARNING``/``ACTIVE`` via
a fresh discovery run. ``DISABLED`` is operator-set only: the learned
preference is never applied and there is no automatic transition out
(FR-014).

VariantBulkUpsertItem.title: VariantBulkUpsertItem
VariantBulkUpsertItem.description:
One variant row nested under a product in `POST /v1/products/bulk-upsert`.

Identity resolution order (FR-011): `external_id` -> `sku` ->
`(product_id, title)` (the parent product_id is filled in by the
router once the parent product's identity resolves).

VariantBulkUpsertItemStandalone.title: VariantBulkUpsertItemStandalone
VariantBulkUpsertItemStandalone.description:
One row in the standalone `POST /v1/variants/bulk-upsert` payload.

Each row names its parent product explicitly via exactly one of
`product_id`, `product_external_id`, or `product_sku` -- resolved
set-based (one scoped lookup, never a per-row query) and
workspace-consistency pre-checked (`app_shared.catalog.consistency`):
a cross-workspace or unresolvable parent reference is rejected
(422), never silently dropped or left to a raw FK-violation 500.

VariantCreate.title: VariantCreate
VariantCreate.description: A single explicit variant on a `POST /v1/products` payload.

VariantResponse.title: VariantResponse
VariantResponse.description: A `product_variants` row as returned by the API.

VariantStatus.title: VariantStatus
VariantStatus.description: Lifecycle status of a ``product_variants`` row (SPEC-04 FR-017).

VariantStrategy.title: VariantStrategy
VariantStrategy.description: Variant-resolution strategy of a ``scrape_profiles`` row (SPEC-06 §22, FR-001).

WebhookEndpointCreate.title: WebhookEndpointCreate
WebhookEndpointCreate.description:
`POST /v1/webhook-endpoints` request body.

`secret`, if supplied, is plaintext on the wire only — the router
encrypts it before storage and never echoes it back (FR-005).

WebhookEndpointResponse.title: WebhookEndpointResponse
WebhookEndpointResponse.description:
A `webhook_endpoints` row as returned by the API.

Every column **except** `secret_encrypted`/`secret_key_version`
(FR-005) — `has_secret` is a derived boolean the router computes
from `secret_encrypted is not None`. Always built via `_to_response`
(explicit field mapping), never `model_validate(orm_obj)`.

WebhookEndpointUpdate.title: WebhookEndpointUpdate
WebhookEndpointUpdate.description:
`PATCH /v1/webhook-endpoints/{id}` — every field optional (partial update).

Distinguishes "omitted" (unchanged) from "explicitly null" via the
router's `exclude_unset=True` dump: an omitted `secret` leaves the
stored ciphertext untouched; `secret: null` clears both
`secret_encrypted`/`secret_key_version`; a non-null `secret` is
re-encrypted. `url`, if present, is re-validated by the router via
`validate_competitor_url` (same `UNSAFE_URL` rule as create).

WebhookEventResponse.title: WebhookEventResponse
WebhookEventResponse.description: A `webhook_events` row — one recorded domain-change event.

WorkspaceDefaultProfileAssignment.title: WorkspaceDefaultProfileAssignment
WorkspaceDefaultProfileAssignment.description:
`PUT /v1/scrape-profiles/workspace-default` request body.

`profile_id: null` clears the workspace's default (FR-012/FR-013).
